-   They should have the workshop folder open in Positron (**File → Open Folder...**) and `student_scripts/Session 6 - Plotting Basics_STUDENT.R` open.

## Teaching notes by part

**Every part.** Build each plot **one layer at a time** and run it after every `+`, so learners see what each layer adds.

**Part 1 — Set up.** The `linelist` lines are already in the student script: learners just run them, then type the measles version (TRY IT 1). Point out that the factor order from Session 5 isn't saved in the `.rds` file, so it has to be set again right after importing — and that `import()` and `mutate()` can go in one pipeline.

**Part 2 — The grammar of graphics.** Run the three steps separately: empty canvas, axes only, then bars. Stress `+` not `%>%` between layers, and that `+` goes at the **end** of the line — the two most common beginner errors. Show the second one live: put `+ geom_histogram()` on its own line and run both lines. The first line draws empty axes, then R stops with *Cannot use `+` with a single argument. Did you accidentally put `+` on a new line?* The ⚠️ box on the lesson page has the same example.

**Part 3 — Histograms.** Point out the "using `bins = 30`" message from the Part 2 plot, then choose `binwidth` yourself. Live-try `binwidth = 1` and `binwidth = 10` so learners see the shape change. The 🔁 `hist()` box after TRY IT 3 is reading only (30 seconds): one line, quick for a first look, but no layers. In TRY IT 3, reassure learners that the "removed rows" warning is just the 29 missing ages.

**Part 4 — Mapping vs setting.** This is the key idea. Ask the class:

-   *What happens if you put `fill = "blue"` inside `aes()`?* Have them try it first. — The bars are pink-red and the legend says "blue": ggplot treated "blue" as data (a column whose every value is the word "blue") and gave it the first default color.

**Part 5 — Scatter plots.** With 6,451 rows, many points overlap — show `size` and `alpha` fixing that. Filtering into `ggplot()` is reading only: point to it on screen 2 and name the switch, `%>%` **into** `ggplot()`, then `+` **between** layers. Learners use it right away in TRY IT 5, and type it in Follow along 6.2. In TRY IT 5, emphasize that a flat trend line ("no relationship") is a result too.

**Part 6 — Box plots.** Walk through the parts of the box (median, IQR, whiskers at 1.5 × IQR, outliers). `stat_summary()` (the mean as a diamond) is reading only: show the plot on screen 2. Learners copy the line in TRY IT 6, which is homework if behind. Ask the class:

-   *Why is the mean (diamond) above the median (line)?* — The ages are right-skewed: a few older patients pull the mean up (female: median 11, mean 12.7; male: median 17, mean 19.5).

Mention `geom_violin()` as an alternative.

**Part 7 — Labels and themes.** TRY IT 7 is a checklist for a presentation-ready plot: a title that states a finding, axis labels with units, a legend title in words, a source caption, and text big enough for the back of the room. Ask two or three learners to share their plot on screen and go through the list together. Point out that a complete theme like `theme_minimal()` resets everything, so it must come **before** `theme(legend.position = ...)`. `base_size = 14` is handy for slides. Early finishers: ⭐ BONUS (fill by `vaccinated`; `geom_violin()`).

**Wrap-up.** Today: `ggplot()`, `aes()`, `geom_histogram()`, `geom_point()`, `geom_smooth()`, `geom_boxplot()`, `labs()`, themes, and the presentation-ready checklist. Next, Session 7 — Plotting further: bar charts, choosing colors, epidemic curves, facets, and saving plots to files.

## TRY IT answers at a glance

The numbers match the TRY IT numbers in the lesson, the student script, and the solutions file. Follow-along prompts are numbered by part (Follow along 5.3 = Part 5, third prompt).

| TRY IT | Answer |
|---|---|
| 1. Import and order the measles data | `import(...) %>% mutate(age_cat = fct_relevel(...), vaccinated = fct_relevel(...))`; `levels(measles$age_cat)` starts with "Under 5" |
| 2. Build a plot in three steps | Step 2 is an empty plot with temperatures on the x-axis; step 3 draws the bars |
| 3. Measles ages | Age 2 has the most cases (102); most cases are ages 1–5; the warning is the 29 missing ages |
| 4. Mapping fill | Small hump near 37 °C = no fever (99); big hump near 39 °C = fever (1064) |
| 5. A scatter plot | `filter(!is.na(days_in_hospital))` gives 427 patients; the trend line is nearly flat |
| 6. A box plot (homework if behind) | Medians 4 days (Yes), 5 (No), 5 (Unknown) — no clear difference |
| 7. Make a plot presentation-ready | Any measles plot with `labs()` (title, axis labels with units, legend title, caption) and a theme with `base_size`, saved as `my_plot` — see the solutions file |
